title: Audit Log Policy Orchestrator Terraform Module (CloudTrail -> OpenSearch/S3 retention + health checks)
creator: Ava Mitchell
description:
Scope:
- Build a reusable Terraform module (redwood_logging_audit_orchestrator) to provision and maintain VPC-scoped audit pipelines for Private deployments. The module will wire CloudTrail -> S3 (encrypted) -> lifecycle -> optional Glacier/Archive, plus OpenSearch ingest (managed domain or cross-account ingest) and index lifecycle policies (ILM).

Functional goals:
- Create opinionated defaults for retention (90d hot, 365d warm, archive to Glacier after 365 days) while allowing overrides per deployment.
- KMS-backed S3 encryption and CloudTrail key rotation support; param to accept existing CMK ARN.
- OpenSearch index lifecycle templates and curator-style rollover that match token/ingest throughput.
- Provide Canary health-checks: a Lambda (or small Fargate task) that verifies CloudTrail delivery, S3 object availability, OpenSearch write/read of a test doc, and emits CloudWatch metrics/alarms.
- Export monitoring dashboards (CloudWatch/OpenSearch) and SLO hints for Console.
- Upgrade strategy: support tfv0.15+ module consumers. Implement a migration tool (terraform state import helpers + documented manual steps) for v1 -> v2 changes.

Configuration surfaces (variables):
- enabled (bool), environment (string), cloudtrail_name (string), s3_bucket_name (string or auto-generated), s3_kms_key_arn (string), opensearch_domain_name (string), retention_days_hot (int), retention_days_warm (int), archive_to_glacier_after_days (int), cross_account_ingest_role_arn (optional), iam_principals (list), lifecycle_transition_rules (map/string), canary_enabled (bool), notification_sns_topic (optional).

Outputs and usage examples:
- Expose outputs for cloudtrail_arn, s3_bucket_arn, kms_key_arn, opensearch_domain_endpoint, canary_lambda_arn. Provide a concrete example in examples/basic with both managed and cross-account ingest patterns.

Acceptance criteria:
- Module passes terraform validate and linting with tfsec suppressed guidelines documented.
- End-to-end test in PR: creates resources in a test account, CloudTrail events are delivered to S3, lifecycle transitions occur, sample documents indexed into OpenSearch by our ingest pipeline.
- Health-check canary publishes a custom CloudWatch metric and a Grafana/Console row shows green/red.
- Migration docs and upgrade guide published in Confluence and linked from README.
- Security review completed and KMS integration verified for key policies.

Rollout plan:
1) Merge module and run CI acceptance in staging accounts.
2) Enable module in one pilot private deployment zone (canary) with short retention override to validate rollbacks.
3) Monitor billing and ingestion dashboards for 2 weeks, then flip to full retention.

Notes on trade-offs and decisions:
- We choose managed OpenSearch (AWS) with VPC endpoints for simplicity; cross-account ingest pattern supported for customers using centralized OpenSearch.
- Canary uses Lambda with minimal IAM scope; if customers require FIPS/HSM strictness, we document alternatives.
- Default retention is conservative for compliance but must be tunable for small customers to reduce costs.

Documentation and artifacts:
- README in module with diagrams and state migration steps.
- Confluence design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Private+Audit+Orchestrator (draft)
- Example PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/terraform-modules/pull/482 (draft)
